You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Procurement (MM-PUR).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: Vendor/supplier master, purchase requisitions, RFQs, purchase orders, goods receipt, invoice verification and 3-way match, approval/release strategies, contracts and scheduling agreements, source determination.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Vendor master (payment terms, currencies, approved items); Requisition -> RFQ -> PO -> Goods Receipt -> 3-way match -> AP bill chain; configurable approval threshold rules stored as data. Contracts, scheduling agreements and source determination are not in the v1 list.

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

## Key Components of SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement

The module covers the entire procurement process, from determining requirements to tendering, supplier selection and contract management to ordering, goods receipt posting and invoice verification.

### Essential Processes

**Contracts and Scheduling Agreements:**
Scheduling agreements in procurement define delivery schedules over a specific period, reducing administrative work needed to create multiple purchase orders. Advanced sourcing scenarios include framework agreements, scheduling agreements, and supplier evaluation.

**Source Determination:**
Procurement teams can automate source determination using source lists, quota arrangements, and condition records.

**Invoice Verification:**
Expertise includes three-way matching, goods receipt posting, and invoice verification procedures. Invoice verification processes are streamlined with automation, enhancing the accuracy of transactions and financial compliance.

**Additional Key Processes:**
The module includes procurement master data management for vendor master records and purchasing info records, purchase requisition processing for creation and approval, and purchase order management including creation and release procedures.

### Integration and Analytics

The module is seamlessly integrated with SAP Finance (FI), Controlling (CO), Supply Chain Management (SCM) and SAP Ariba, so all procurement data is recorded centrally and coordinated with financial and logistics processes.

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive overview of SAP S/4HANA MM-PUR procurement key capabilities:

## Release Strategy

The release strategy defines the approval process for purchase requisitions. The strategy specifies the release codes with which a complete purchase requisition or a requisition item must be released (approved) and the sequence in which approvals have to be given. You can assign a maximum of eight release codes to the release strategy.

In SAP S/4HANA, you can set up approval procedures for purchase requisitions and for external purchasing documents, such as purchase orders, contracts, scheduling agreements, and requests for quotations.

## Release Procedures

The system supports two main release procedures:

1. **Release Procedure Without Classification**: This Procedure is applicable only for Purchase Requisitions (PR). Here PR is released Item by Item only.

2. **Release Procedure With Classification**: This procedure is applicable to Purchase Requisitions (PR), Purchase Order (PO), Contract and Scheduling Agreements. Item by Item and Header level releases can be configured.

## Purchase Requisition Overview

A purchase requisition is a request or instruction to Purchasing to procure a certain quantity of a material or a service so that it is available at a certain point in time.

## 2025 Enhancements

The SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 release for Sourcing and Procurement introduces several valuable enhancements, most notably the new SAP Fiori app "My Purchase Requisitions – New."

Service items (product type Service) now include Start Date and End Date fields to define the service period, replacing the single Delivery Date field. This feature enables accurate representation of services as Services are delivered over a period but not on one day.

I've completed the web search on your query. Here's a summary of the key findings related to SAP S/4HANA business partner, supplier master, MM logistics, invoice verification, three-way matching, tolerance, and blocking:

## Key Findings:

**Business Partner & Supplier Master in S/4HANA:**
Payment terms, incoterms, and partner functions (e.g., Ordering Address, Goods Supplier, Invoicing Party) are maintained in the Supplier (Purchasing) role. Blocking logic allows you to block at BP central level (no usage anywhere), Supplier (FI) (no postings), or Supplier (Purchasing) (no POs).

**Three-Way Match Process:**
3-way matching in SAP is an invoice verification process that cross-references an invoice with its corresponding purchase order (PO) and goods receipt (GR) before authorizing payment, ensuring that businesses only process payments for goods or services that were properly ordered, received, and invoiced at the correct amount.

**Tolerance and Blocking:**
If price, quantity, or amount fall outside the tolerance keys configured in customising (transaction OMR6), MIRO either warns the user or blocks the invoice for payment. Supplier-specific tolerances can be configured (OMRX) where if the master record of the vendor contains a tolerance group for invoice verification, these settings take priority.

**Invoice Verification in MM:**
The three-way matching process is primarily managed within the Materials Management (MM) module, which oversees procurement and inventory functions.

content.content:
# SAP S/4HANA Sourcing & Procurement Certification Topic Areas

Based on the certification guide, the C_TS452 exam covers these functional areas:

## Core Topic Areas with Weightings

| Topic | Weight | Coverage |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Master Data | 20-25% | "Vendor management, material master, purchasing info records" |
| Procurement Processes | 35-40% | "Purchase requisitions, purchase orders, approval workflows" |
| Goods Receipt & Invoice | 20-25% | "Three-way matching, GR/IR clearing, invoice verification" |
| Advanced Features | 15-20% | "Framework agreements, supplier evaluation, analytics" |

## Specific Capabilities

The learning journey addresses:

- **Master Data Configuration**: Vendor records, purchasing information records, material master setup
- **Purchase Requisition Processing**: Creation, approval workflows, and conversion procedures
- **Purchase Order Management**: Creation, release procedures, change management
- **Receipt & Verification**: Three-way matching processes and invoice verification
- **Advanced Sourcing**: "Framework agreements, scheduling agreements, and supplier evaluation"
- **Integration & Analytics**: Connections with Materials Management, Financial Accounting, and Controlling modules

The guide emphasizes that "understanding how sourcing and procurement integrates with other SAP modules" distinguishes consultant-level expertise from basic end-user knowledge.

input.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, SAP Learning/certification syllabi, and consulting sources), completed June 2026. In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), Sourcing and Procurement (MM-PUR) covers the full procure-to-pay cycle: business-partner-based supplier master data, purchasing info records, purchase requisitions (now with Fiori self-service apps), RFQs and quotation comparison, purchase orders, goods receipt, and logistics invoice verification with 3-way match, tolerances, and payment blocking. Approvals run through either classic classification-based release strategies or the newer flexible workflow, applicable to PRs, POs, contracts, scheduling agreements, and RFQs. Framework agreements (quantity/value contracts, scheduling agreements with delivery schedules), source determination (source lists, quota arrangements, info records), and supplier evaluation round out the area; certification weightings confirm master data, the PR-to-PO process, and GR/invoice verification as the practitioner-essential core. Atlas v1 plans the essential discrete P2P chain end-to-end but deliberately defers outline agreements, automated source assignment, and supplier evaluation.

capabilities.description: BP-based supplier records with purchasing and company-code views: payment terms, currency, partner functions, and blocking at central/FI/purchasing levels.
capabilities.later_path: Later add partner functions (ordering address vs. invoicing party) and granular block levels.

capabilities.description: Vendor-material master data holding time-dependent prices/conditions, planned delivery times, and tolerances used to default PO data; 20-25% of the certification master-data weighting.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 'approved items' on the vendor master captures the vendor-item link but not time-dependent pricing conditions or lead-time data that S/4HANA info records default into POs.
capabilities.later_path: Extend the vendor approved-items table with price, valid-from/to, and lead-time fields and use them to default PO lines.

capabilities.description: Internal demand documents (manual or MRP-generated) requesting a quantity of material/service by a date, converted to RFQs or POs; 2025 adds the 'My Purchase Requisitions - New' Fiori app and service-period items.
capabilities.later_path: MRP-generated requisitions arrive when the manufacturing/planning module lands.

capabilities.description: Request quotations from multiple suppliers, record quotations, compare prices, and convert the winning quote into a PO.
capabilities.later_path: Multi-bidder price-comparison views and rejection letters can be layered onto the v1 RFQ document.

capabilities.description: The central external purchasing document with item-level pricing, delivery dates, account assignment, change management, and output to suppliers; anchors PO history (GR/IR).
Receipt posting referencing the PO that updates stock and valuation, writes PO history, and feeds GR/IR clearing for the 3-way match.
capabilities.later_path: Atlas plans GR in the v1 chain; stock/valuation postings are owned by the inventory module.

capabilities.description: Match supplier invoice against PO and goods receipt, apply tolerance keys, block payment on variance, and post the AP liability with GR/IR clearing.
capabilities.later_path: Configurable tolerance groups, invoice-release workflow, and ERS (evaluated receipt settlement) are natural follow-ons; AP posting itself lives in finance.

capabilities.description: Classification-based release strategies (up to 8 release codes keyed on value, plant, material group, doc type) plus the newer flexible workflow, covering PRs, POs, contracts, scheduling agreements, and RFQs.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans data-driven value-threshold rules only; S/4HANA's essential release strategy also keys on multiple characteristics (plant, material group, document type), supports multi-step approver chains, and applies to more document types than the PR/PO chain.
capabilities.later_path: Generalize the threshold-rule schema into condition records (field/operator/value) with ordered multi-approver steps applied per document type.

capabilities.description: Longer-term agreements with target quantity or value against which release orders draw down, with header/item conditions and release documentation.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from the Atlas v1 list; v1 covers only the discrete requisition-to-PO chain with no outline-agreement document type or drawdown tracking.
capabilities.later_path: Add a contract document type referencing vendor and items with committed qty/value, and let POs reference it as release orders that consume the commitment.

capabilities.description: Outline agreements with delivery schedule lines (often MRP-maintained, with JIT/forecast releases) replacing many discrete POs in repetitive/direct procurement.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from Atlas v1; no document exists for schedule lines or releases, so repetitive direct-procurement scenarios are not supported in v1.
capabilities.later_path: Model as a contract variant carrying dated schedule lines that goods receipts consume directly, added alongside MRP integration.

capabilities.description: Automatic proposal/assignment of supply sources (info records, contracts, source lists, quotas) to requisitions, enabling automated requisition-to-PO conversion.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1's vendor-master 'approved items' provide manual approved-source data, but there is no automatic source proposal on requisitions, no quota arrangements, and no contract/info-record sources to determine against.
capabilities.later_path: Add a source-assignment service that matches open requisition lines to approved vendor items (later contracts) and supports one-click or automatic PO creation.

capabilities.description: Scoring suppliers on price, quality, and delivery performance plus embedded Fiori analytics (procurement overview, spend KPIs).
capabilities.reason: Not in the Atlas v1 plan; classed by SAP itself as an advanced feature (15-20% certification weighting) and not required to run the core P2P cycle.
capabilities.later_path: Compute supplier scorecards from existing GR (on-time/quantity) and invoice (price variance) history in the reporting module.

content.text: Done. The structured assessment for Procurement (MM-PUR) has been returned: 12 capabilities covering the full P2P scope, with 6 rated full (supplier master, requisitions, RFQ, PO, goods receipt, 3-way match), 3 partial (info records, release strategies, source determination), and 3 out-of-scope (contracts, scheduling agreements, supplier evaluation), each with reasons and later paths.
